source: CARE Cambodia (Pailin), "TIP Training on Maize Production" / បទដ្ឋានអនុវត្ដបច្ចេកវិទ្យា ផលិតកម្មដំណំពូតក្របម, 2009. Funded by AusAID (ACIMA project), the European Union (Pailin Food Security Program), and ACIAR (CCPMP project).
text:
Choosing the right location is critical for successful corn (maize) production. Corn grows well on land with a fertile topsoil layer at least 0.8 meters deep, or deeper. Farmers should avoid planting corn on steeply sloped land, because sloped fields are prone to erosion and runoff, which strips away soil fertility over time to the point where the land can no longer support crop production.

Farmers should also avoid planting corn on low-lying, flood-prone land. Corn has weak tolerance for waterlogging, and prolonged flooding can seriously damage the crop. The source document illustrates this with side-by-side photos: corn growing poorly/failing on waterlogged soil versus corn growing vigorously on fertile, well-drained soil.
